Subject: GroundSite: K8s I/O segmentation & node-slice ownership — planning sync

Hi Alex (+ GroundSite infra team),

Thanks again for walking us through the site constraints yesterday. Per our call, I put together a short agenda for a technical sync focused on cluster-level I/O segmentation, node-slice ownership, and persistent volume ownership boundaries so we can produce a recommended cluster layout. Key objectives for the session: 

- Clarify tenant isolation model (single cluster multi-tenant vs. multi-cluster per tenant).
- Define node pool roles, CPU/GPU/IO sizing, and eviction/QoS expectations.
- Agree on persistent volume mapping (ephemeral vs. blockstore) and encryption/retention policies.
- Identify network egress/NAT constraints and any firewall rules that affect storage traffic.

Please attach any IOPS/latency SLOs you have for the inference workloads and a list of tenant identifiers with approximate pod density. I attached a draft PV mapping sheet and our latest network diagram for reference.

Proposed time: Tue 2026-11-30 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite linked).

Questions for GroundSite before the call:
1) Can you confirm whether tenant-A needs block-level snapshots retained for 90+ days?
2) Any on-prem KMS/HSM for key wrapping or do we integrate with your cloud KMS?
3) Are local NVMe devices available on all nodes or only specific racks?

Attachments: groundsite-pv-mapping.xlsx, network-diagram-v2.png

Vanessa — thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few quick answers ahead of tomorrow's sync: 

- Tenant-A requires snapshots for 120 days; we currently snapshot to our on-site NFS backup cluster.
- KMS: we have an HSM appliance in rack 7; prefer HSM integration for root key material.
- NVMe: NVMe is available on GPU nodes in racks 2–4 only; CPU-only nodes have SATA SSDs.

I'll upload our workload profile CSV to the Drive folder you linked. Two other constraints: we have a hard 2 Gbps inter-rack egress cap per tenant and a firewall rule that blocks outbound SMB to 10.0.0.0/8 (affects backup target).

Appreciate if your team can sketch a node-pool mapping that accounts for NVMe locality and snapshot placement. See inline on the PV mapping sheet for examples.

Thanks Alex — useful constraints. Quick notes from an ops perspective before the call: 

- Cluster topology suggestion (initial):
  * control-plane: 3 dedicated control-plane nodes (no workloads) — use SATA SSDs with etcd backups offsite.
  * nvme-workload-pool: GPU+NVMe nodes (racks 2–4) — for low-latency model inference and cached KV stores. Use local ephemeral volumes for model cache, but persist critical state to blockstore in the same rack when possible.
  * cpu-general-pool: CPU nodes with SATA SSDs for background processing, batch ingest, and CI/testing.
  * backup-proxy-pool: small set of nodes that handle snapshot bundling and push to on-site NFS backup (to respect firewall/egress rules).

- PV mapping guidance:
  * model-cache: emptyDir or local persistent volume (ephemeral), mounted on NVMe nodes only. No snapshot retention required.
  * state-store: RWO block volumes provisioned from rack-local blockstore, encrypted with HSM-wrapped keys — snapshot retention 120d for tenant-A.
  * logs/metrics: use cluster-level aggregation to remote object store; short-term buffer on SATA SSDs.

- QoS & eviction: mark model-serving pods as high QoS (Guaranteed) by pinning requests/limits. Ensure eviction thresholds on nodes respect reserved system and kubelet eviction signals for disk and inode pressure.

Open questions for call:
- Do you want a single StorageClass with topology-aware provisioning or separate StorageClasses per rack? Topology-aware will simplify scheduling but increases PV management complexity.
- Are there regulatory constraints around snapshot storage location (on-site vs. encrypted blob in cloud)?

I've updated the attached PV mapping sheet with suggested StorageClass names and a rack affinity column.

Quick technical follow-ups before the meeting: 

- Locality trade-offs: If we strictly bind model-serving pods to racks 2–4 NVMe nodes, we get excellent p99 token latency but reduced scheduling flexibility during maintenance. Propose a mixed approach: a small guaranteed NVMe-only pool (for latency-sensitive replicas) plus burstable GPU slots in adjacent racks with network-mounted block PVs for fallback.

- Eviction policy: recommend explicitly reserving ~1.5Gi per pod for model-cache to avoid eviction due to sudden cache growth. Use PodDisruptionBudget for critical replicas.

- Snapshot mechanics: prefer offloading snapshot creation to backup-proxy-pool nodes to avoid snapshot I/O hitting primary NVMe devices. These proxies can pull snapshot deltas and stream to the NFS backup target (workaround for SMB block) — avoids firewall egress issues.

- CSI & encryption: validate that the chosen CSI driver supports topological provisioning with HSM-wrapped key references; if not, we need a controller-side wrapper. I will bring a short checklist to the call.

A few action items we should confirm during the sync:
1) whether GroundSite prefers storage topology (per-rack StorageClass) or a single cross-rack StorageClass with topology hints.
2) retention windows per tenant and whether they accept encrypted off-site blob copies (if cloud fallback is needed).

Karthik

Appreciate the fast responses — good prep ahead of the sync. Quick summary of decisions we captured during today's meeting and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Decisions: 
- Topology: go with two StorageClasses — "nvme-local-sc" (topology-constrained to racks 2–4) and "rack-block-sc" (per-rack blockstore via CSI) for stateful workloads. This gives predictable locality for p99-sensitive paths and fallback for scheduling.
- Snapshots: tenant-A snapshot retention set to 120 days; snapshot creation handled by backup-proxy-pool to avoid saturating NVMe nodes.
- KMS/HSM: GroundSite HSM will be integrated for root key wrapping; we will use HSM references in our CSI encryption keys.
- QoS: model-serving pods tagged Guaranteed; reserve disk and memory; PodDisruptionBudgets for critical sets.

Action items: 
1) Redwood (Laura/Karthik) to produce an updated PV mapping and StorageClass YAMLs (due 2026-12-03). Attached: updated groundsite-pv-mapping.xlsx.
2) GroundSite (Alex) to confirm HSM API endpoints and provide sample service account creds for staging (due 2026-12-02).
3) Redwood (Vanessa/Marissa) to draft an ops-runbook covering snapshot run cadence and recovery steps (first draft due 2026-12-07).

Meeting notes and assets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GroundSiteDesign (I added the diagram and PV sheet).

If there are any corrections to the decisions above, please reply-all and we'll update the runbook. Otherwise we'll proceed with the action item deadlines above.

Thanks — see you on the implementation thread.
